sources.name: JSON-LD 1.1
sources.role: JSON-based Linked Data serialization, context, IRI expansion, compaction, flattening, framing and remote-context interpretation contract
verified_facts: JSON-LD 1.1 is a W3C Recommendation defining a JSON-based serialization for Linked Data.
A JSON-LD context maps terms to IRIs and influences datatype, vocabulary, base-IRI and value interpretation.
Expansion applies a context so IRIs, types and values are expanded; compaction applies a supplied context to reshape the document.
semantic_limits: Valid JSON-LD syntax, expansion or compaction establishes a standards-conformant representation, not source authority, completeness or physical truth.
Remote or imported contexts can change term interpretation; exact context bytes, resolved URLs, processing mode and digests must be pinned for reproducible evidence.
A JSON-LD numeric literal must not create a parcel-height row without authoritative source bytes, exact cadastral polygon, CRS, vertical datum, units, algorithm and execution receipts.

sources.name: RDF Dataset Canonicalization
sources.role: RDFC-1.0 deterministic blank-node labeling, canonical N-Quads serialization, graph-isomorphism comparison and hashing contract
verified_facts: RDFC-1.0 converts an RDF dataset into a canonicalized dataset by assigning deterministic identifiers to blank nodes.
The algorithm produces a canonical N-Quads form and by default uses SHA-256 for internal hash computations.
Isomorphic RDF datasets are expected to produce the same canonically labeled list of quads.
semantic_limits: Canonical equality or a canonical hash establishes graph-level equivalence under the selected algorithm, not factual accuracy, authority or completeness.
Canonicalization does not prove equality of original downloaded byte streams, transport completeness or source publication identity.
A signed or hashed RDF dataset must not become terrain evidence without pinned input object, algorithm version, exact polygon, CRS, vertical datum, units and measurement receipts.

sources.name: Data on the Web Best Practices
sources.role: dataset metadata, provenance, quality, versioning, persistent identifiers, standardized formats and publication-practice contract
verified_facts: The Recommendation provides domain-independent best practices for publishing and consuming data on the Web.
It recommends metadata, provenance, data-quality information, version indicators and persistent URIs for datasets and their contents.
It recommends machine-readable standardized formats and guidance that improves discovery, reuse and trust.
semantic_limits: A publisher claiming best-practice alignment does not itself prove that complete provenance, quality evidence or immutable source bytes were supplied.
A persistent URI identifies a dataset resource but does not guarantee an immutable version unless version identity and object digest are separately pinned.
Metadata, quality labels and provenance descriptions must not substitute for actual parcel geometry, elevation source, vertical datum and execution receipts.

sources.name: Model for Tabular Data and Metadata on the Web
sources.role: annotated table, row, column, cell, datatype, parsing, foreign-key and validation contract
verified_facts: The Recommendation defines an annotated tabular data model that abstracts rows, columns, cells and metadata from exchange syntax.
Datatype annotations and formats guide parsing and validation of cell values.
Tables can declare foreign keys whose referenced rows are checked during validation.
semantic_limits: Successful datatype parsing or table validation establishes conformance to the declared table model, not source authority or real-world correctness.
Foreign-key integrity proves only declared relational consistency and does not prove cadastral identity, spatial containment or measurement provenance.
A numeric cell typed as decimal or number must not become a parcel-height result without exact source bytes, geometry, CRS, vertical datum, units, method and execution receipts.
